subject: ent
title: Nasal Septum, Lateral Nasal Wall, and Ostiomeatal Complex

steps.tx: The nasal septum divides the nasal cavity into symmetrical right and left air passages, constructed from an osteocartilaginous framework lined by mucoperichondrium and mucoperiosteum. The primary cartilaginous component is the quadrilateral septal cartilage. The osseous septum is formed superiorly by the **perpendicular plate of the ethmoid** bone and posteroinferiorly by the vomer, supported along its base by the maxillary and palatine crests.
steps.say: The nasal septum comprises the quadrilateral cartilage anteriorly, perpendicular plate of ethmoid posterosuperiorly, and vomer posteroinferiorly.

vis.alt: Sagittal anatomical section of the nasal septum showing ethmoid plate, vomer, and septal cartilage
vis.caption: Osteocartilaginous framework of the nasal septum and primary vascular anastomotic territories. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: On the anteroinferior portion of the nasal septum sits Little area, the most vascular site in the nasal cavity and the source of over ninety percent of all epistaxis episodes. Within Little area, four arterial systems anastomose to construct **Kiesselbach plexus**. This vascular network represents a critical confluence between the internal carotid circulation (via anterior ethmoidal branches) and external carotid circulation (via sphenopalatine, greater palatine, and superior labial branches).
steps.say: Little area on the anterior septum contains Kiesselbach plexus, the origin of ninety percent of nosebleeds. It unites internal and external carotid arterial branches.

vis.title: Component Arteries of Kiesselbach Plexus
rows: Enters via anterior naris over philtrum

steps.tx: In contrast to anterior Little area, posterior epistaxis originates from **Woodruff plexus**, situated on the lateral nasal wall immediately posterior and inferior to the posterior end of the middle turbinate. Composed of prominent anastomosing venules and terminal branches of the sphenopalatine artery, posterior bleeding from Woodruff plexus is common in elderly hypertensive patients, requiring posterior packing or sphenopalatine artery ligation.
steps.say: Woodruff plexus on the posterior lateral nasal wall is the source of severe posterior epistaxis in elderly hypertensive patients, often requiring posterior packing.

left.title: Little Area (Kiesselbach Plexus)
points: Anterior epistaxis in children and young adults.
Controlled with direct pressure or chemical cautery.

right.title: Woodruff Plexus
points: Located on lateral nasal wall behind middle turbinate.
Posterior epistaxis in elderly hypertensive patients.
Hidden from direct anterior view; blood flows down throat.
Requires posterior balloon packing or surgical ligation.

steps.tx: The lateral nasal wall features three downward-curving scroll-like bony shelves designated turbinates or conchae: superior, middle, and inferior. The inferior turbinate is a separate, independent cranial bone, whereas the middle and superior turbinates are integral appendages of the ethmoid labyrinth. Beneath each turbinate lies a corresponding air passage or meatus. The **inferior meatus** receives the opening of the nasolacrimal duct, guarded by the mucosal valve of Hasner.
steps.say: Three turbinates line the lateral wall. The inferior turbinate is an independent bone; beneath it opens the nasolacrimal duct guarded by the valve of Hasner.

vis.alt: Anatomical schematic showing turbinates, meatuses, and paranasal sinus drainage openings
vis.caption: Lateral nasal wall architecture showing paranasal sinus drainage ostia within respective meatuses. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: The middle meatus is the physiological hub of paranasal sinus ventilation and mucociliary clearance. It receives drainage from the anterior ethmoidal air cells, the frontal sinus (via the frontonasal duct), and the maxillary sinus (via the primary maxillary ostium). The superior meatus receives drainage from the posterior ethmoidal cells, while the sphenoid sinus empties into the **sphenoethmoidal recess** superior and posterior to the superior turbinate.
steps.say: The middle meatus receives the frontal, maxillary, and anterior ethmoid sinuses. The superior meatus drains posterior ethmoids, and the sphenoethmoidal recess drains the sphenoid.

steps.tx: The ostiomeatal complex (OMC) is the critical functional anatomical unit located in the middle meatus that coordinates ventilation and mucociliary clearance of the anterior sinus group. It comprises the **uncinate process**, the ethmoidal infundibulum, the ethmoidal bulla, and the curved two-dimensional drainage slit termed the hiatus semilunaris. Edema, mucosal contact, or anatomical variations within the ostiomeatal complex obstruct drainage, triggering recurrent acute rhinosinusitis.
steps.say: The ostiomeatal complex in the middle meatus comprises the uncinate process, ethmoid bulla, and hiatus semilunaris. Obstruction here leads directly to sinusitis.

nodes.label: Hiatus Semilunaris & Middle Meatus Common Pathway

steps.tx: The uncinate process is a delicate, sickle-shaped sagittal bony leaflet that projects posteroinferiorly from the lateral nasal wall, forming the medial boundary of the ethmoidal infundibulum. During functional endoscopic sinus surgery, an **infundibulotomy** (uncinectomy) is the fundamental primary step. Resecting the uncinate process fully exposes the natural maxillary sinus ostium and opens access to the anterior ethmoidal bulla.
steps.say: The sickle-shaped uncinate process bounds the infundibulum. In functional endoscopic sinus surgery, uncinectomy is the mandatory initial step to open the sinuses.

left.title: Uncinate Process Attachment to Lamina Papyracea
points: Infundibulum ends superiorly in blind terminal recess.
Frontal sinus drains directly into middle meatus.

right.title: Uncinate Attachment to Skull Base or Middle Turbinate
points: Infundibulum opens superiorly into frontal recess.
Frontal sinus drains directly into the infundibulum.

steps.tx: The ethmoidal bulla represents the largest and most constant anterior ethmoidal air cell, projecting medially into the middle meatus immediately posterior to the uncinate process. The crescentic curved gap between the posterior margin of the uncinate process and the anterior surface of the bulla is the **hiatus semilunaris**, which serves as the narrow anatomical doorway leading into the ethmoidal infundibulum.
steps.say: The ethmoid bulla is the largest anterior ethmoid cell. The curved slit between the uncinate process and bulla is the hiatus semilunaris, leading into the infundibulum.
